what: The eight limbs, the definition of yoga as restraint of citta's activities, the list of obstacles (vyādhi, ālasya, pramāda, bhrānti-darśana, anavasthitatva...) and the reversal 'powers in emergence, obstacles in samādhi'

evidence.detail: LiP 1.8.7 'yogo nirodho vṛtteṣu cittasya' ~ YS 1.2; LiP 1.9.1-13 and ŚiP 7.2.38.1-8 ~ YS 1.30-31; LiP 1.9.52 ~ YS 3.37
VP 6.7.36-37 yamas and niyamas as in YS 2.30-32

what: The order of creation from pradhāna/prakṛti through mahat, ahaṃkāra, tanmātras, elements and senses; puruṣa and pradhāna as principles (here forms of Viṣṇu)
Upaniṣadic verses and images reused in the Purāṇas

evidence.detail: MkP 39.63 ~ ŚvetU 2.13 (first signs of yoga); MkP 42.7 ~ MuU 2.2.4 (bow and arrow; MkP reads 'prāṇo dhanuḥ'); BhP 1.2.21 = MuU 2.2.8; VP 6.7.28 = Brahmabindu Up. 2 (direction unsettled for the minor Upaniṣad); GP 2.10.75 leech image ~ BĀU 4.4.3

what: Sāṃkhya-yoga dialogues and Kṛṣṇa narrative shared with the epic and its Harivaṃśa

evidence.detail: Brahma Purāṇa 243-245 parallels the Vasiṣṭha-Karāla Janaka dialogue of MBh 12; VP book 5 parallels the Harivaṃśa

what: The Garuḍa Pretakalpa reuses verses of the Mārkaṇḍeya's account of dying and the road of Yama (MkP 10.48-78) within the same tradition
Pāśupata yoga and vow in the Śaiva Purāṇas (Liṅga, Vāyu, Kūrma, Śiva)

evidence.detail: LiP 1.7.54, 1.88.6-30, 2.55.26 name 'pāśupata yoga'; ŚiP 7.1.33 Paśupati-vrata; Upamanyu gives Kṛṣṇa Pāśupata initiation

what: The Sātvata/Pāñcarātra doctrine of Vāsudeva and the four vyūhas in the Vaiṣṇava Purāṇas
The Lalitopākhyāna's narrative of Lalitā, Bhaṇḍāsura and Śrīpura, and the Brahmāṇḍa attribution of the Lalitā Sahasranāma

evidence.detail: the Sahasranāma's colophon names the Brahmāṇḍa Uttarakhaṇḍa, Hayagrīva-Agastya dialogue

what: The Bhāgavata as root scripture: Kṛṣṇa as Bhagavān himself (1.3.28), the rāsa-līlā and the gopīs' love, the nine forms of devotion, the name as the dharma of Kali

evidence.detail: Gauḍīya authors (Rūpa, Jīva) build on BhP 1.3.28, 7.5.23-24, 10.29-33, 11.14

what: Ṛṣabha, the first Tīrthaṅkara of the Jains, appears in the Bhāgavata as an avatāra and avadhūta; the Bhāgavata adds a polemical account of the 'Arhat' king
